output.reason: Sudden painless monocular vision loss described as a curtain, persisting two hours, requires immediate emergency assessment for retinal artery occlusion, retinal detachment or other stroke-equivalent cause.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Sudden, painless loss of vision in one eye that has not returned can be a stroke-equivalent or retinal emergency needing urgent eye and stroke assessment today. Have someone drive you rather than driving yourself; if you develop face or limb weakness, trouble speaking, or become unsteady, call 911 immediately.
differential: Central retinal artery occlusion (retinal stroke equivalent)

redFlags.concern: Sudden painless monocular vision loss, persistent
redFlags.quote: About two hours ago I suddenly lost vision in my right eye, it was like a curtain coming down over it.

redFlags.concern: Weakness, speech difficulty or other neurologic deficits
Headache or jaw claudication (giant cell arteritis features)

output.vitalSigns: No blood pressure, heart rate or other readings reported; whether any measurement occurred is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Sources are emergency-department reference syntheses without fundoscopic or visual-acuity findings for this patient, so the specific cause is unresolved.

citations.claim: Sudden, painless, monocular vision loss is the presentation of central retinal artery occlusion, a stroke equivalent.
citations.limitation: No visual acuity, RAPD or fundoscopic examination reported, so CRAO is not established.

citations.claim: CRAO and retinal detachment both present with painless monocular vision loss and differ in urgency and treatment, requiring fundus examination.
citations.limitation: Distinguishing features require in-person examination or imaging not available remotely.
